globalconfigurationinfo-text: Note: Global configuration options with .wslconfig are only available for distributions running as WSL 2 in Windows Build 19041 and later. Changes take effect after WSL restarts.
absolutewindowspath-text: An absolute Windows path to a custom Linux kernel. Backslashes have to be doubled, e.g. C:\\kernel\\vmlinux.
memoryinfo-text: How much memory to assign to the WSL 2 VM. Default: 50% of the total memory on Windows. A plain number is bytes; add MB or GB for other units, e.g. 8GB.
processorinfo-text: How many logical processors to assign to the WSL 2 VM. Default: the same number of logical processors Windows has.
wildcardinfo-text: Whether ports bound to wildcard or localhost inside the instance can be reached from Windows via localhost:port. Default: on.
swapinfo-text: How much swap space to add to the WSL 2 VM, 0 for no swap file. Swap storage is disk-based RAM used when memory demand exceeds limit on hardware device. Default: 25% of the memory on Windows, rounded up to the nearest GB. (e.g. 8GB, 512MB)
vhdinfo-text: An absolute Windows path to the swap virtual hard disk. Default: %Temp%\swap.vhdx.
guiinfo-text: Boolean to turn on or off support for GUI applications (WSLg) in WSL. Default: on.
consoleinfo-text: Boolean to turn on an output console window that shows the contents of dmesg upon start of a WSL 2 distro instance. Default: off. Only available for Windows 11.
nestedvirtinfo-text: Boolean to turn on or off nested virtualization, enabling other nested VMs to run inside WSL 2. Default: on. Only available for Windows 11.
vmidleinfo-text: The number of milliseconds that a VM is idle, before it is shut down. Default: 60000. Only available for Windows 11.

diskofflinehint-text: Hint: The disk might be online in Windows. Set it to Offline in Disk Management and try again.
unknownmounterror-text: Unknown error occurred during mount operation.
kernelmodulesinfo-text: An absolute Windows path to a custom Linux kernel modules VHD.
safemodeinfo-text: Run WSL in "Safe Mode" which disables many features and is intended to be used to recover distributions that are in bad states. Only available for Windows 11 and WSL version 0.66.2+.
maxcrashdumpcountinfo-text: Set the maximum number of crash dump files that will be retained. Default: 10.
dnsproxyinfo-text: Configure the DNS server in Linux to the NAT on the host. Default: on. Only applicable when the networking mode is nat; turning it off mirrors the DNS servers from Windows to Linux instead.
networkingmodeinfo-text: How WSL connects to the network: none, nat, bridged, mirrored or virtioproxy. Default: nat, which an unrecognised value also falls back to. bridged has been deprecated since WSL 2.4.5.
firewallinfo-text: Allow Windows Firewall rules to filter WSL network traffic, including the Hyper-V traffic of the WSL 2 VM. Default: on.
dnstunnelinginfo-text: Changes how DNS requests are proxied from WSL to Windows. Default: on.
autoproxyinfo-text: Enforces WSL to use Windows' HTTP proxy information. Default: on. Only available for Windows 11.
defaultvhdsizeinfo-text: Limit the maximum size a distribution file system is allowed to take up. Default: 1099511627776 (1 TB). A plain number is bytes; add MB, GB or TB for other units.
automemoryreclaiminfo-text: How WSL gives unused memory back to Windows: disabled, gradual or dropCache. Default: dropCache, which an unrecognised value also falls back to.
sparsevhdinfo-text: When set to true, any newly created VHD will be set to sparse automatically. Default: off.
besteffortdnsparsinginfo-text: Attempt to resolve DNS requests ignoring unknown records. Default: off. Only applicable when dnsTunneling is set to true.
dnstunnelingipaddressinfo-text: Specifies the nameserver for DNS tunneling. Default: 10.255.255.254. Only applicable when dnsTunneling is set to true.
initialautoproxytimeoutinfo-text: How long, in milliseconds, to wait for the HTTP proxy information before starting the distro. Default: 1000. Only applicable when autoProxy is set to true, and the WSL instance has to be restarted to use the retrieved proxy settings.
ignoredportsinfo-text: Ports Linux applications can bind to even if they are used in Windows, as a comma-separated list, e.g. 3000,9000,9090. Only applicable when the networking mode is mirrored.
hostaddressloopbackinfo-text: Allow the container to connect to the host by its assigned IP address. Default: off. Only IPv4 addresses assigned to the host are supported. Only applicable when the networking mode is mirrored.
byok-info-text: Use your own OpenAI-compatible API key for AI Chat. This only affects the AI Chat assistant — AI Workspace tools (Hermes Agent, OpenClaw, Open WebUI) run locally in WSL and are not affected.

defaultuserinfo-text: The default user of this distro, stored in /etc/wsl.conf. Unlike "Start user" above, this applies to every way the distro is started, not only launches from this app, and it is kept when the distro is exported.
wslconfrestart-text: Restart this distro to apply the changes
ignoredinmirrored-text: Ignored when the networking mode is mirrored.
unitexample-text: e.g. 8GB, 512MB or a plain number of bytes
bootsystemdinfo-text: Use systemd as the init system in this distro. Requires WSL 0.67.6 or newer. The default depends on the distro.
bootcommandinfo-text: A command run as root every time this distro starts, e.g. service docker start. Its output is not shown, and a failure does not stop the distro.
automountenabledinfo-text: Automatically mount the Windows drives under the mount root. Default: on.
automountmountfstabinfo-text: Mount the entries of /etc/fstab when the distro starts. Default: on.
automountrootinfo-text: The directory the Windows drives are mounted under. Default: /mnt/, so C: becomes /mnt/c.
automountoptionsinfo-text: Comma-separated DrvFs options for the Windows drives: uid, gid, umask, fmask, dmask, metadata and case. umask, fmask and dmask have no effect unless metadata is set as well. Example: metadata,uid=1000,gid=1000,umask=22
networkgeneratehostsinfo-text: Let WSL generate /etc/hosts from the Windows host. Default: on.
networkgenerateresolvconfinfo-text: Let WSL generate /etc/resolv.conf with the DNS servers of the Windows host. Turn this off to keep your own DNS configuration. Default: on.
networkhostnameinfo-text: The hostname of this distro. Defaults to the Windows computer name.
interopenabledinfo-text: Allow this distro to start Windows executables. Default: on. Requires Windows 10 1809 or newer.
interopappendwindowspathinfo-text: Append the Windows PATH to the Linux PATH so Windows programs can be called by name. Default: on.
gpuenabledinfo-text: Make the Windows GPU available inside this distro. Default: on.
usewindowstimezoneinfo-text: Keep this distro's time zone in sync with the Windows one. Default: on.
protectbinfmtinfo-text: When on, WSL keeps its own binfmt registration for Windows interop and systemd cannot replace it. Turning it off hands the registration to systemd, which can stop Windows programs from running inside this distro. Default: on. Requires Windows 11 or Server 2022.
settingoutofrange-text: Outside the supported range (%s), so it is shown as text and saved exactly as written.
settinginvalidsize-text: Not a size WSL understands. Use a plain number of bytes, or add KB, MB, GB or TB.
startuserinfo-text: Only applies to terminals this app starts. To change the user every other way of starting this distro gets, use the User setting below.
wslconfwritefailed-text: Could not write "%s" to /etc/wsl.conf. The setting was not applied.
wslinbox-text: Inbox build (does not report a version)
updatewslwebdownloadinfo-text: Downloads the update directly instead of through the Microsoft Store. Use this when the Store is blocked.
wslconfigwritefailed-text: Could not write .wslconfig. The changed settings were not saved.
requireswsl-text: Requires WSL %s or newer. These actions are not available on the installed build.
diskallocatedinfo-text: Size of ext4.vhdx on the Windows drive. It grows as the distro fills up and never shrinks on its own.
diskusedinfo-text: What the distro's own file system reports. The gap to the allocated size is what can be reclaimed.
diskusageunavailable-text: The usage could not be read. The distro has to be able to start for this.
resizediskinfo-text: Grow the virtual disk. Whole numbers only, with B, MB, GB or TB - 2.5TB is not a valid size. WSL is shut down first.
resizediskinvalid-text: Not a size WSL accepts. Use a whole number with B, MB, GB or TB; decimals are not supported.
setsparseinfo-text: Makes this distro's existing disk sparse, so space freed inside it is returned to Windows. This is not the sparseVhd option in the global settings, which only affects distros created afterwards.
sparsefailed-text: The sparse setting could not be changed: %s
movenative-text: This runs wsl --manage --move, a single supported operation. The distro is never unregistered.
movelegacy-text: The installed WSL has no move command, so the distro is exported to a file, unregistered and imported again. Do not close the app while this runs.
custompackageinfo-text: Package a distro as a .wsl file, or install one. A .wsl file is a root filesystem archive plus an /etc/wsl-distribution.conf that tells Windows how to set the distro up on first launch: the out-of-box experience, the default user, the Start menu shortcut and the Windows Terminal profile.
custompackageunsupported-text: Building and installing .wsl packages needs the Microsoft Store build of WSL. Update WSL from the global settings screen.
distributionconfinfo-text: Read from and written to /etc/wsl-distribution.conf in the selected distro. The export below freezes these values into the package, so set them first.
distrounreachable-text: This distro could not be read. Start it once, or pick another one.
oobedefaultnameinfo-text: The name the distro is registered under. Required for a .wsl file to install by double-click; installing with a name overrides it.
oobecommandinfo-text: Runs the first time an interactive shell opens in the installed distro. A non-zero exit counts as failure and the user cannot open a shell, so test it before packaging.
oobedefaultuidinfo-text: The UID the distro starts as. Set it to 1000 when the first-run command creates an account, and use the same UID in both places.
writeoobescriptinfo-text: Writes Microsoft's sample account-creation script to /etc/oobe.sh, makes it executable, and points the first-run command and the default user ID at it.
shortcutenabledinfo-text: Whether installing the package adds a Start menu entry. On by default.
shortcuticoninfo-text: Path inside the distro to an .ico file of at most 10 MB. WSL's own icon is used when this is not set.
terminalprofileenabledinfo-text: Whether installing the package adds a Windows Terminal profile. On by default.
terminalprofiletemplateinfo-text: Path inside the distro to a JSON fragment used as the terminal profile. The name and command line are filled in by WSL. A default profile is generated when this is not set.
packagereadinessinfo-text: Checked against Microsoft's recommendations for a custom distribution.
packageready-text: This distro is ready to package.
packagenodefaultname-text: No default name is set, so this package cannot be installed by double-clicking it.
packageoobenotexecutable-text: The first-run command %s is not executable inside this distro. The installed distro would refuse to open a shell.
packagenooobe-text: No first-run command is set. The installed distro starts as root and never asks for a user account.
packagenouid-text: A first-run command is set but no default user ID. If the command creates an account, set both to 1000.
packageiconformat-text: The shortcut icon must be an .ico file of at most 10 MB.
packagenowslconf-text: This distro has no /etc/wsl.conf. A packaged distro should carry one, at minimum to state whether systemd starts.
packageresolvconf-text: /etc/resolv.conf is present. WSL generates this file, and shipping one bakes in DNS settings that will be wrong on other machines.
packagedistroinfo-text: Exports the whole root filesystem of the selected distro. This takes minutes and produces a file about as large as the distro; the distro is stopped first so the archive is consistent.
packageformatinfo-text: gzip is the recommended format. Other formats risk breaking compatibility with older WSL versions.
packagenopath-text: Enter a path for the package file
installfromfileinfo-text: Unlike Import, this honours the package's /etc/wsl-distribution.conf, so the new distro gets its first-run setup, its default user, its Start menu shortcut and its terminal profile.
errorenterusername-text: Please enter a username for the default user, or turn the option off.
unsavedchanges-text: This page has changes you have not saved yet. Save them before leaving?
ai-chat-pro-required-text: AI Chat is a Pro feature.
distrostoppedinfo-text: Reading the settings of %s means reading /etc/wsl.conf from inside it, which starts the distro. It stays running until you terminate it.
startandread-text: Start it and read the settings
